summary: Quick sync on POC results, validated latency/cost tradeoffs, and agreed next steps for rollout. Focus: canary strategy, monitoring, runbook, and security sign-offs.
transcript: Header: 2026-12-08 10:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego (SE), Lena (CSM) - Maya, Tom, Iris, Ben (AcmeFin)
00:00 - Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — review last week's perf numbers, talk canary, monitoring, runbook, next steps
00:12 - Maya: Thanks, yeah we ran the afternoon load test and have the results, curious about the dedicated pool sizing you suggested

00:20 - Diego: Great. So the benchmark sheet I put together — I'll share the link after — shows tail latency at 99th percentile at about 220ms for the 4k token endpoint on the optimized quantized model
00:35 - Tom: That 220ms was on your hosted instance, right? When we ran it in our VPC it spiked to 450ms with our network egress settings

00:48 - Diego: Correct, the 220ms is Redwood-hosted with nginx fronting; in VPC there are extra network hops and our KV cache affinity needs to be tuned. We recommended a small affinity change, and that should shave ~120ms
01:05 - Ben: Walk me through the canary approach — we want zero blips for payment flows, so how do we do canary vs A/B without risking error rates

01:14 - Ava: Good question. We recommend a staged canary: 1% traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool variant A for 24h, then 5% for 6h, then 20% for 2h with automated rollback triggers. Canary includes health checks on latency, error rate, and output quality score from your evaluation set
01:35 - Maya: Output quality score — is that automatic or do we need to run evals each time?

01:40 - Diego: Redwood can run the eval harness automatically using your golden prompt set — we compute a delta metric and alert if drift exceeds threshold. It's in Console as "quality monitoring", though sometimes the transcript spells it like "qual monitor"
02:00 - Iris: For security we need full KMS integration and that logs key access. Can you confirm Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys and audit logs?

02:08 - Lena: Yup, Redwood Private supports bring-your-own KMS, HSM hooks, and the control plane records audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 artifact pack, but note we're not a legal team — it's a pointer, not a replacement for your compliance review
02:26 - Iris: Okay also we need proof of separation between training data and inference logs — PII concerns. Does Redwood redact or persist full prompts by default?

02:35 - Ava: By default we don't retain user prompts beyond X days for hosted accounts, but for Private you control retention. You can also enable prompt redaction and token-level masking — Diego, can you add the doc reference?
02:45 - Diego: Yep will add link to security pack and config snippets for redaction and KMS in the runbook
03:10 - Tom: Monitoring — what dashboards should our SREs watch during canary? We want simple thresholds to avoid paging for expected transient spikes

03:18 - Diego: Console has per-route latency, per-model token cost, error counts, and traces. For canary we suggest 3 dashboards: latency percentile (p50/p95/p99), errors (5xx/timeout), and quality-delta. Set alerts: p99 > 500ms for >2m, error rate >0.5% in a 5m window, or quality-delta >3%
03:40 - Ben: About rollout automation — do you have a built-in canary controller or is it manual?

03:45 - Ava: We have a rollout feature in Console for canary/A-B with guardrails and automated rollback by policy. Many customers use it with their CICD to trigger traffic shifts; Diego can demo the policy rules in another session if useful
04:05 - Maya: We need to plan a dry-run with our on-call SREs — want to simulate a rollback scenario too
04:12 - Tom: Agreed, dry-run to rehearse failover and rollback steps, plus validate runbook run time

04:20 - Diego: For cutover planning the runbook includes pre-cutover validation (load test baseline, config sync), cutover steps (DNS TTL, traffic shift percentages), rollback criteria, and post-cutover checks (SLOs, cost burn rate). I'll send a v1 runbook
04:40 - Iris: A quick note on network — our infra team wants to ensure private subnets allow egress to Redwood control plane. Any IP ranges we should whitelist?
04:50 - Ava: We'll share the list. For Private deployments there's an option to operate air-gapped but for VPC you typically whitelist a small range and use a private peering link
05:05 - Ben: Can we talk about cost during canary? If we route 20% traffic to Dedicated, are we billed proportionally or is there a base committed capacity?

05:14 - Ava: For pilots we recommend a small dedicated pool with burst capacity; billing is committed capacity plus actual usage for burst. We'll include sample cost math in the pricing note — but roughly you'll see a small baseline + marginal token cost
05:30 - Maya: On the model side, Diego suggested quantization to 4-bit for most flows — any quality regressions seen?

05:36 - Diego: We did AB tests on your eval set; 4-bit offers 1-2% quality delta on certain prompts, but latency improves ~30%. We recommended using 4-bit for non-critical paths and fallback to 8-bit or fp16 for payment-critical route
06:00 - Tom: Fallback — does Redwood support automatic model fallback on quality or latency triggers?

06:07 - Diego: Yes, you can configure routing policies: if latency > threshold or quality-delta exceeds X, route to alternate model variant or to hosted fallback. This is part of the smart routing we discussed previously
06:30 - Ben: For runbook ownership, who signs off on pre-cutover check? AcmeFin SRE or product?
06:35 - Maya: SRE will own the technical sign-off, product owns go/no-go for feature flags
06:42 - Ava: We'll include a sign-off checklist with owner fields — Diego to add to runbook
07:00 - [Link share] Diego: Sharing benchmark sheet: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/acmefin-poc (note: placeholder link)
07:20 - Iris: On audit and log retention, can we set log retention to 90 days and export to our SIEM?
07:26 - Lena: Yes, Console supports log export to S3 or GCS and can be streamed to SIEM. Retention is configurable per-tenant
07:40 - Maya: One risk: if the KV cache warms differently in Prod than in POC, we might get different latencies. How do we mitigate?
07:48 - Diego: Mitigation: pre-warm cache during dry-run, use static affinity for routing, and run a pre-cutover synthetic load to populate caches. We'll add those steps to runbook
08:10 - Tom: What about database connection limits or downstream rate limits? We need to ensure Redwood's concurrency profile doesn't burst DB connections

08:18 - Diego: We recommend adding a concurrency limiter at the route and using batching settings. Redwood has token-aware batching that reduces downstream calls; Diego to include recommended concurrency and batch size
08:40 - Ben: Quality monitoring — how often will the eval run? Real-time or batch?
08:45 - Diego: Usually batch every 1 hour for the eval set and daily aggregate for alerts, but can be near-real-time for smaller golden sets
09:05 - Maya: Ok, timeline — we want to be live by end of month if dry-run looks good. Is that still feasible?
09:10 - Ava: Yes, with these action items and security checklist we can aim for 2026-12-21 cutover window. Dry-run mid-week prior
09:20 - Iris: We'll need the SOC2 and encryption config by Friday to start our compliance review
09:25 - Ava: Understood, Lena will send the pack and Diego will add KMS runbook snippets
09:40 - Ben: A small ask — can we have an A/B variant where 10% traffic gets model variant B with more conservative quantization to measure quality delta in prod?
09:48 - Diego: Absolutely, we can configure an A/B experiment in Console and capture the quality delta. That fits into the canary stage
10:05 - Maya: Any concerns about data residency? Some of our EU users need regional processing
10:10 - Ava: Redwood can route EU traffic to EU region by policy. For Private you can deploy in-region. We'll document routing policy config
10:25 - Tom: Final: let's confirm the dry-run date. How about 2026-12-17 09:00 PST?
10:30 - Maya: Works for me, SREs confirm on slack
10:36 - Ava: Great. Recap of next steps: Diego send runbook + benchmarks, Ava send pricing + cutover checklist, Iris to send security questions. We'll reconvene after dry-run prep
10:45 - [Meeting end]
